description: Every `function` row must have been visited by the function-metrics enricher. `param_count` is the witness: the enricher stamps it unconditionally, even for a zero-argument function, so a function row that cannot answer it is a row no enricher examined. The booleans the same gate stamps are written only when TRUE, so such a row answers neither `has_todo = 'true'` nor `= 'false'` — it is missing from both sides of the question rather than answered wrongly on one, which is what let it go unnoticed. Python broke this until 0.188.0: `decorated_definition` was mapped to `function` and named after the definition it wraps, whose span is already folded back to the leading decorator, so the two rows were indistinguishable to the dedupe and the wrapper survived — 36,978 of 141,233 rows on pytorch, 26%. Held here for the four languages the golden corpora cover (C, C++, Rust, Python); a language outside them is unpinned. Each case pins an absolute count, so a corpus re-pin moves a pair together while a parity break moves only one of the two.

cases.name: every_python_function_row_was_enriched_on_pytorch
cases.description: The corpus the defect was found on. Both totals must be the same number; if they part again, some Python function shape is producing a row the metrics gate does not recognise.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE language = 'python' WHERE fql_kind = 'function' LIMIT 1

cases.name: control_pytorch_python_functions_all_answer_param_count
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE language = 'python' WHERE fql_kind = 'function' WHERE param_count >= 0 LIMIT 1

cases.name: every_python_function_row_was_enriched_on_zephyr
cases.description: A second, independent Python population — the defect was 20% here, so one corpus agreeing is not evidence.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE language = 'python' WHERE fql_kind = 'function' LIMIT 1

cases.name: control_zephyr_python_functions_all_answer_param_count
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE language = 'python' WHERE fql_kind = 'function' WHERE param_count >= 0 LIMIT 1
